key_insight: 3D opto-electro-thermal simulation shows MgXS3 (X = Ti, Zr, Hf) lead-free chalcogenide perovskites can deliver high-efficiency solar cells when thickness, doping, and defect density are jointly optimized.
engineering_relevance: The work provides device-design guidance for realistic multilayer solar architectures, showing how a BSF layer and thermal-carrier coupling can improve collection and stability.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer
Parameter sweep of absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and Sb2S3 BSF effects
evidence_signal: Under optimized conditions, simulated PCE reaches 28.18% for MgZrS3, 26.72% for MgTiS3, and 28.16% for MgHfS3, with corresponding Voc, Jsc, and FF values reported.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based and depend on assumed material parameters, so experimental validation and defect/interface realism are needed before device deployment.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
